title: Global Electric Vehicle Component Architecture Outlook 2025–2030
summary: A deep-dive investigation into OEM component sourcing, modular architectures, and supply chain bottlenecks shaping EV commercialization.
body:
The shift toward electric mobility requires rethinking automotive component ecosystems. Drawing from ground-truth interviews with 85 Tier-1 and Tier-2 suppliers across Asia and Europe, this report maps market volume, price sensitivity, and supplier transition timelines.

Key Findings:
- Modular skateboards are standardizing battery enclosure designs across 70% of new passenger platforms.
- Thermal management systems represent the highest margin expansion opportunity for specialty chemical and fluid producers.
- Supply chain reshoring mandates will drive localized sourcing by an estimated 28% through 2028.
author: Chromatus Automotive Practice

title: De-Risking New Market Entry: A Primary Fieldwork Framework
summary: Why desk research fails high-stakes market entry decisions, and how structured ground investigations establish actual willingness-to-pay.
body: Too many organizations enter new territories based on top-line macroeconomic assumptions. This whitepaper outlines Chromatus’s four-stage engagement framework that tests demand elasticity, channel partner margins, and regulatory friction before capital is committed.
author: Vijay Natekar & Ameya Dingare

title: How a Global Conglomerate Validated Commercial Solar Adoption Across Tier-2 Indian Cities
summary: Pinpointing real rooftop solar adoption hurdles among industrial cluster owners across 14 manufacturing hubs.
body:
A renewable energy developer required ground-level verification of whether commercial rooftop solar adoption incentives were translating into signed contracts.

Methodology:
Chromatus deployed field researchers to conduct 320 structured CAPI interviews with factory owners, power dispatchers, and state utility liaisons.

Outcome:
The client revised their commercial leasing model, reducing customer acquisition costs by 34% and securing 45MW in industrial commitments within two quarters.
author: Rahul Nawale
